{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  unit_tests:
    name: unit tests
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            url: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/nightly/nvim-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
            manager: sudo snap
            packages: go
          - os: ubuntu-22.04
            url: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/stable/nvim-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
            manager: sudo snap
            packages: go
          - os: ubuntu-22.04
            url: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/v0.11.0/nvim-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
            manager: sudo snap
            packages: go
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "^1.24.0" # The Go version to download (if necessary) and use.
      - run: date +%F > todays-date
      - name: Restore cache for today's nightly.
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: _neovim
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ matrix.url }}-${{ hashFiles('todays-date') }}

      - name: Prepare
        run: |
          ${{ matrix.manager }} install --classic ${{ matrix.packages }}
          # sudo apt install go
          test -d _neovim || {
            mkdir -p _neovim
            curl -sL ${{ matrix.url }} | tar xzf - --strip-components=1 -C "${PWD}/_neovim"
          }
          GO111MODULE=on go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest

          mkdir -p ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/nvim-lua/plenary.nvim ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start/plenary.nvim
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ray-x/guihua.lua ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start/guihua.lua
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start/nvim-treesitter
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kyazdani42/nvim-web-devicons ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start/nvim-web-devicons
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start/nvim-lspconfig
          ln -s $(pwd) ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/vendor/start
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          export PATH="${PWD}/_neovim/bin:${PATH}"
          nvim --headless -u tests/minimal.vim -c "TSInstallSync go" -c "q"
          make test
",
  "rationale": "The workflow currently has no job-level timeout, which can lead to runaway CI consumption if a job hangs. Historical runs show a median duration of ~2 minutes, so a 10-minute timeout provides ample headroom (5x) while protecting against stuck jobs. This optimization is supported by pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (literature and experiment evidence) which reports up to 26.8% elapsed time savings in a measured fork. The change preserves all test coverage and matrix configurations.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

We are given a workflow that runs unit tests on multiple OS configurations (matrix). The workflow currently has `fail-fast: false` in the matrix strategy. We have evidence for several patterns, including P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure) and P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout). We also have evidence for caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) but the workflow already uses a cache for neovim nightly.

We need to decide which optimization is supported by evidence and fits the workflow.

Looking at the workflow:
- It runs on three matrix configurations (different OS and neovim versions).
- The matrix strategy has `fail-fast: false`.
- There is no explicit timeout for the job.

Potential optimizations:
1. Change `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true` (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST). This would cancel remaining matrix jobs if one fails. However, we must consider if the repository requires all matrix outcomes. The pattern's contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". We don't know if the repository requires all matrix outcomes. The workflow is for unit tests, and typically you might want to see all failures. But the pattern evidence shows it can save resources. The experiment examples show it passed in synthetic scenarios. However, we need to check if the repository has any required checks that would be violated. The required_checks in repository_context is empty. But we don't know the policy. The pattern says we must evaluate the contract before changing cancellation. Since we don't have evidence that the repository requires all matrix outcomes, we might consider it. But we must be cautious.

2. Add a custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). The workflow currently has no timeout. The pattern suggests setting a custom timeout based on historical successful durations. We don't have historical data, but we can set a reasonable timeout. The pattern's preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". We don't have that data, but we can look at the CI history: the runs show durations of about 2 minutes (from created_at to updated_at). For example, the first run: 2026-10-12T09:53:21Z to 2026-10-12T09:55:15Z -> about 1 minute 54 seconds. Others are similar. So a timeout of, say, 5 minutes might be safe. However, the pattern requires measuring false timeout failures. We don't have that data. But we can propose a timeout with headroom.

3. The workflow already caches the neovim download. It uses a cache key based on the URL and today's date. That's a form of caching. The pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is about caching dependency downloads. The workflow already does that. So no change needed.

The repository might want to see all results. The pattern's contraindications include "Every matrix outcome is required". We don't know if that's the case. The required_checks is empty, but that doesn't mean they don't require all matrix outcomes. The pattern's safety tests include "Inject one failing matrix cell" and "Verify required matrix result policy". We cannot verify the policy. So it might be risky.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: The workflow has no timeout. The jobs run for about 2 minutes. Setting a timeout of, say, 10 minutes would prevent runaway jobs. The pattern's contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". We can set a limit with headroom (e.g., 5x the median). The median is ~2 minutes, so 10 minutes is safe. The pattern's preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have 5 successful runs, all around 2 minutes. That's representative. The pattern's safety tests include "Cold dependency installation", "A deliberately hung step", "Slow valid run". We can't test, but we can set a reasonable timeout.

The evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT includes an experiment example (batch-interactive-three) that showed a 26.8% elapsed savings. That's a measured benefit. The evidence for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST includes synthetic experiments that passed, but the limitations say "Synthetic workload: timings are scenario resource costs, not original repository CI savings." So it's less directly applicable.

Given the above, I think adding a custom timeout is a safer and more directly supported optimization. The workflow currently has no timeout, and the pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is applicable.
